items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: And Danny, he wasn't practicing between shows

ctx.x: He'd already heard Charlie and he was raving and everything about this guy that runs the G-minor 7th against a C 7th, and that gives you your flatted fifth, your flatted seventh, your flatted ninth, and all that, you know. Because he was there telling me all of this, you know? He

was telling me this when he come back raving. And we were pretty good pals, you know, in the band. And he was raving about this, and we said, "What can it be?" We'd never heard of the thing. "Yeah, but this guy is playing something else." So now he's telling me all about it. He was trying to show me how it goes, and I said, "Yeah, but like two and two is four, you know." And he said, "No, not exactly." So now he gets enough nerve to get up on the stand, and he had a chorus of "Some of These Days," and so he gets…

wanted to see what he was doing, you know. Anyhow, we always walked around together between shows. So now he's showing it to me, and he says, "Jonah, you see this? And if you get here and you've got this chord going too long, just sit there playing the straight F chord. Play that chord one bar. You've got four bars after it, then go to F-sharp and come back to F again, you know." And I said, "Yeah, it's interesting." So I get on the stand with "Some of These Days," and I made one of these things, and Cab said,…
